group_assessment.counts_measured: PubMed esearch 2026-10-03 (tool=LEGEND-research): 'Chang NS[au]' 138, 'Chang NS[au] AND WWOX' 66, 'Hsu LJ[au]' 103, 'Hsu LJ[au] AND WWOX' 30.
group_assessment.weighting: Five of the six papers in this group come from one laboratory lineage (Chang N-S / Hsu L-J, National Cheng Kung University). That laboratory originated WWOX and carries the gene's largest single output, so its measurements carry full weight; what it does NOT carry is independence. Two of its subjects are exclusive to it: 'Zfra NOT Chang NS[au]' returns 1 record and that record is an unrelated zebrafish androgen-receptor paper matching the string by accident; 'TIAF1 NOT Chang NS[au]' returns 5 of 20. The autophagy axis is the opposite case and is the reason this group is readable as a contradiction at all: 'WWOX AND autophagy' returns 10 records and 8 of them are from neither Chang NS nor Hsu LJ.
group_assessment.note: Research-group knowledge base is excluded from the public edition; this rests on measured PubMed counts and on the papers' own author lists.

field_density.note: WWOX is NOT the subject. It appears three times: as a yeast-two-hybrid positive control (WOX1/p53), and twice as cited background for the TGF-beta1/Hyal-2/WOX1/Smad4 route. No WWOX manipulation, no WWOX readout.

entries.proposition: WWOX IS NOT MEASURED IN THIS PAPER. Its only substantive appearance in the Results is as cited background for the TGF-beta1/Hyal-2 route; no WWOX manipulation and no WWOX readout exists here. A claim that this paper supports a WWOX statement is a claim about its reference 14, not about its data.
entries.snippet: TGF-β1 binds membrane hyaluronidase type 2 (Hyal-2) for recruiting tumor suppressor WW domain-containing oxidoreductase (WOX1) (also named WWOX or FOR) and Smad4 to relocate to the nuclei
entries.anchor: Results, 'TGF-β1-induced TIAF1 self-binding occurs independently of TβRII', sentence 2

entries.proposition: THE HUMAN DATA ARE CROSS-SECTIONAL PREVALENCES IN TWO GROUPS THAT DIFFER BY ~21 YEARS OF AGE, AND TIAF1 AGGREGATION ITSELF IS NOT MORE COMMON IN THE DEMENTED GROUP. The age difference is in the authors' own sentence and is never controlled.
entries.snippet: TIAF1 aggregation was present in 59.0% of postmortem nondemented human hippocampi (age 59.0±17.0, n=41), and 54% in older postmortem AD patients (age 80.0±8.8, n=97)
entries.anchor: Results, 'TIAF1 aggregates are abundant in the hippocampi of nondemented humans', filter-retardation paragraph

entries.proposition: THE 17% VERSUS 48% FIGURES ARE CONDITIONAL PREVALENCES WITHIN TIAF1-POSITIVE SAMPLES, NOT A TIME COURSE. The brief that selected this paper quotes them as the human evidence that TIAF1 aggregation precedes amyloid; the source states them as a proportion, with no longitudinal sampling and no statistical test reported in this paragraph.
entries.snippet: Further analysis revealed that there was only 17% of the total TIAF1-positive samples possessing Aβ aggregates in the control group, and 48% for the AD group.
entries.anchor: Results, 'TIAF1 aggregates are abundant in the hippocampi of nondemented humans', final sentence

entries.proposition: THE DIRECTION OF THE Thr668 EFFECT IS SPLIT BETWEEN THE ABSTRACT AND THE RESULTS. The abstract says aggregation leads to DEphosphorylation; the Results say overexpressed TIAF1 INCREASED Thr668 phosphorylation and that TGF-beta1 is what suppresses it. Anything carried from this paper must carry the two-step form.
entries.snippet: Importantly, phosphorylation of endogenous APP at Thr668 was significantly increased in cells overexpressing TIAF1/TIAF1, and that TGF-β1 suppressed the phosphorylation
entries.anchor: Results, 'TIAF1 self-aggregation precedes production of Aβ and amyloid fibrils', SK-N-SH paragraph
